lessons: Guide says never take an off-colour flier over an on-colour one; I took Moon Heron, Murder of Crows and Stitched Drake, then ran WR with only Abbey Griffin and Voiceless Spirit as evasion.
Guide says aim for five removal; my WR ran four (Brimstone Volley, Urgent Exorcism, Ghostly Possession, Traitorous Blood) and lost 1-2 to RG and 0-2 to WG.
Guide says WR needs one flexible late card like Rally the Peasants; I had none, leaning on Scourge of Geier Reach and three Tormented Pariah through grinds of 38 and 18 turns.

Red-green's four removal spells (Harvest Pyre, Prey Upon, Rolling Temblor, Spidery Grasp) carried a 2-1 record, so take flexible removal over filler like Cobbled Wings, which I took twice and never played.
Cutting black entirely left my RG deck without answers to the UB deck's two Claustrophobia and Victim of Night, which beat me 2-1, so keep one black or enchantment-proof answer.
Black flowed at this table, with seat 3's UB deck going 3-0, so before committing to red-green, take strong black removal over a marginal fifth green creature.
Darkthicket Wolf at pick 2 led nowhere: Festerhide Boar, Kindercatch and Gnaw to the Bone were speculative picks that never made my WU deck, so commit to a lane by mid pack 1.
Tonight contradicted the guide's claim that WU spirits is the strongest archetype: my fliers went 1-2, losing 0-2 to UB's two Claustrophobia and 0-2 to WR's Elder Cathar and Tormented Pariah humans.
Armored Skaab and Stitcher's Apprentice need self-mill to work, as the guide warns, so they were dead weight in my non-UG deck; play playable fliers or two-drops instead.
Blue-black fliers with two Claustrophobia and Victim of Night as removal went 3-0 here, so take cheap removal like Claustrophobia over a second Delver of Secrets, which I cut anyway.
Seat 1's RG deck (Prey Upon, 2x Reckless Waif, 2x Villagers of Estwald) ended one of my games in just 11 turns, so prioritise early blockers over a fourth expensive flier.
Black was crowded: seat 4 BR and seat 7 UB shared my colour, so take black removal earlier in pack 1 rather than relying on pack 3 picks like Victim of Night.
Tonight's BR, with eight removal spells, went 0-3 in 18-to-32-turn grinds, contradicting the guide's removal-plus-bodies recipe; fliers and finishers must close.
Rotting Fensnake is on the skip list yet made my BR deck; cut it for a flier or removal spell, since my ground bodies won none of six games.
The guided 3-0 BR won with Sever the Bloodline and Into the Maw of Hell, cards my 0-3 BR never drafted; prioritise them over fillers.
Tonight's games ran 11 to 22 turns, so card quality beat curve speed; take Smite the Monstrous and Into the Maw of Hell over marginal 2-drops.
Round three's 1-2 loss to UB, facing two Claustrophobia and Victim of Night, suggests a 15-creature board is fragile; keep the second Rage Thrower over a marginal 2-drop.
Round two's 19- and 22-turn wins were grindy, so prioritize fliers like Angel of Flight Alabaster and Angelic Overseer over ground filler when stalled boards decide games.
Rally the Peasants is absent from the guide's white commons, yet seat 5 beat me 2-0 with two copies; I took one and left it out of my deck, so play it in white decks.
The guide calls WR humans aggressive, but seat 5's deck won 19- and 22-turn games with Divine Reckoning, so expect longer games against white.
Avacyn's Pilgrim and cheap two-drops carried my WG deck to 2-1 with 4-2 in games, so prioritise cheap creatures over expensive top-end.

Take hard removal for big green threats over tempo 2-drops: Sensory Deprivation, Grasp of Phantoms and Tribute to Hunger did not stop Boneyard Wurm or Scourge of Geier Reach, and the RG round went 29 and 22 turns.
Don't spend late picks on Dream Twist: I took two in pack 2 and cut both, so a playable creature or cheap interaction would have helped the deck more.
Count finishers before building blue-black tempo: Bloodgift Demon and Morkrut Banshee were my only real top end, and the 14- and 23-turn games show the deck needs more threats to close.
